Hangul · advanced

Pronunciation tips
batchim
final consonant
Only 7 sounds survive at the end of a syllable: k, n, t, l, m, p, ng. 옷 sounds like 'ot', 꽃 like 'kkot'.

Survival phrases
Hello
Polite default greeting, any time of day.
A: 안녕하세요, 처음 뵙겠습니다.
B: 네, 안녕하세요! 반갑습니다.
Hello, nice to meet you for the first time. / Hi! Nice to meet you.

Survival phrases
Thank you
Formal. Casual: 고마워 (gomawo).
🗣 [감사함니다] 비음화
A: 도와주셔서 감사합니다.
B: 아니에요, 별말씀을요.
Thank you for helping. / Not at all.

Survival phrases
I'm sorry
Formal apology. 미안해 (mianhae) = casual.
🗣 [죄송함니다] 비음화
A: 늦어서 죄송합니다.
B: 괜찮아요, 저도 방금 왔어요.
Sorry I'm late. / It's fine, I just got here too.

Survival phrases
How much is it?
Point at the item and ask.
A: 이거 얼마예요?
B: 만 이천 원이에요.
How much is this? / 12,000 won.

Survival phrases
Where is the bathroom?
어디예요 = where is.
A: 저기요, 화장실 어디예요?
B: 저쪽으로 쭉 가시면 돼요.
Excuse me, where's the bathroom? / Go straight that way.

Survival phrases
This one, please
Ordering or shopping. 주세요 = please give.
A: 뭐 드릴까요?
B: 이거 주세요. 포장이요.
What can I get you? / This one, to go.

Survival phrases
It's okay / I'm fine
Also used to politely refuse.
🗣 [괜차나요] ㅎ 탈락
A: 괜찮아요? 다쳤어요?
B: 네, 괜찮아요.
Are you okay? Hurt? / Yes, I'm fine.

Survival phrases
Please speak slowly
Lifesaver phrase.
A: 죄송한데 천천히 말해 주세요.
B: 아, 네. 천천히 할게요.
Sorry, please speak slowly. / Ah, sure, I'll slow down.

Survival phrases
I don't speak Korean well
Buys you patience.
🗣 [한구거 잘 모태요] 연음, 격음화
A: 한국어 잘하시네요!
B: 아니에요, 아직 잘 못해요.
Your Korean is good! / No, I'm still not good.

Survival phrases
Just a moment / excuse me
Squeezing past someone on the subway.
🗣 [잠시마뇨] 연음
A: 잠시만요, 지나갈게요.
B: 네, 가세요.
Excuse me, coming through. / Go ahead.

Survival phrases 2
Excuse me (to get attention)
Call a waiter or stop a stranger. Not an apology.
A: 저기요! 메뉴판 좀 주세요.
B: 네, 잠시만요.
Excuse me! The menu, please. / Yes, one moment.

Survival phrases 2
Please help me
Emergency or just a heavy bag.
A: 저기요, 좀 도와주세요.
B: 네, 뭐가 필요하세요?
Excuse me, please help me. / Sure, what do you need?

Survival phrases 2
Please say it again
다시 = again.
A: 죄송한데 다시 말해 주세요.
B: 지하철역은 왼쪽이에요.
Sorry, say that again please. / The subway station is on the left.

Survival phrases 2
Can you speak English?
할 수 있다 = can do.
🗣 [영어 할 수 이써요] 연음
A: 영어 할 수 있어요?
B: 조금요. 천천히 말할게요.
Can you speak English? / A little. I'll speak slowly.

Survival phrases 2
What is this?
Point and ask. Works for food, signs, everything.
A: 이게 뭐예요?
B: 떡볶이예요. 조금 매워요.
What is this? / Tteokbokki. It's a bit spicy.

Survival phrases 2
Do you take cards?
돼요 = is it possible / does it work.
A: 카드 돼요?
B: 네, 돼요. 여기 꽂아 주세요.
Do you take cards? / Yes. Insert it here.

Survival phrases 2
What's the wifi password?
비밀번호 = password.
A: 와이파이 비밀번호가 뭐예요?
B: 영수증에 있어요.
What's the wifi password? / It's on the receipt.

Survival phrases 2
I'm lost
길 = road/way. 잃다 = to lose.
🗣 [기를 이러써요] 연음, ㅎ 탈락
A: 길을 잃었어요. 여기가 어디예요?
B: 여기 홍대예요. 어디 가세요?
I'm lost. Where is this? / This is Hongdae. Where are you going?

Asking around
Where is the bathroom?
Full form. Short: 화장실 어디예요? Both fine.
🗣 [화장시리 어디에 이써요] 연음

Asking around
Could you take a photo for us?
Extra polite with 주실래요. Hand over the phone after.
🗣 [사진 좀 찌거 주실래요] 연음
A: 혹시 사진 좀 찍어 주시겠어요?
B: 네, 그럼요. 하나, 둘, 셋!
Would you mind taking a photo? / Of course. One, two, three!

Introductions
I'm ___
Look at the last Hangul block: 이에요 after a final consonant (저는 킴이에요), 예요 after a vowel (저는 리사예요).

Introductions
What's your name?
Polite: 성함이 어떻게 되세요? for elders or formal settings.
🗣 [이르미 뭐예요] 연음
A: 이름이 뭐예요?
B: 저는 키이예요. 이름이 뭐예요?
What's your name? / I'm Kii. What's yours?

Introductions
Nice to meet you
Lit. 'glad because we met'. Formal: 반갑습니다.
A: 만나서 반가워요.
B: 저도 반가워요.
Nice to meet you. / Nice to meet you too.

Introductions
Where are you from?
에서 = from. 어디 = where.
🗣 [어디에서 와써요] 연음
A: 어디에서 왔어요?
B: 미국에서 왔어요. 오클라호마요.
Where are you from? / From the US. Oklahoma.

Introductions
How old are you?
Normal question in Korea; it decides how people speak to each other.
🗣 [멷 사리에요] 받침 → ㄷ, 연음
A: 실례지만 나이가 어떻게 되세요?
B: 스물여덟이요. 그쪽은요?
Excuse me, how old are you? / 28. And you?

Introductions
What do you do?
일 = work. 직업이 뭐예요? also works.
A: 무슨 일 해요?
B: IT 회사에서 일해요.
What do you do? / I work at an IT company.

Introductions
I'm studying Korean
공부하다 = to study. Say this and people light up.
🗣 [한구거 공부해요] 연음
A: 한국어 공부해요?
B: 네, 매일 조금씩 해요.
Do you study Korean? / Yes, a little every day.

Introductions
What's your hobby?
취미 = hobby. 제 취미는 운동이에요 = my hobby is working out.
A: 취미가 뭐예요?
B: 달리기하고 음악이요.
What's your hobby? / Running and music.

Introductions
Please take care of me
Said after introducing yourself at work or in a group. No English equivalent.
🗣 [잘 부탁드림니다] 비음화
A: 오늘부터 같이 일하게 됐어요. 잘 부탁드립니다.
B: 네, 저도 잘 부탁드려요.
I'm starting work with you today. Please take care of me. / Likewise.

Small talk
How have you been?
Standard greeting for someone you haven't seen in a while.
🗣 [잘 지내써요] 연음
A: 오랜만이에요! 잘 지냈어요?
B: 네, 덕분에요. 잘 지냈어요?
Long time no see! How've you been? / Good, thanks. You?

Small talk
How are things lately?
요즘 = these days. 어때요 = how is it.
A: 요즘 어때요?
B: 바빠요. 그래도 재밌어요.
How are things lately? / Busy. But fun.

Small talk
So-so
Lit. 'it's just like that'. Very common honest answer.
A: 요즘 어때요?
B: 그냥 그래요. 바쁘기만 해요.
How are things? / So-so. Just busy.

Small talk
Nice weather, isn't it
네요 ending = noticing something out loud. 날씨가 춥네요 = it's cold, huh.
🗣 [날씨가 존네요] 비음화, 받침 중화
A: 오늘 날씨가 좋네요.
B: 네, 산책하기 딱 좋아요.
Nice weather today. / Yes, perfect for a walk.

Small talk
What are you doing this weekend?
주말 = weekend, 에 = on.
🗣 [주마레 뭐 해요] 연음
A: 주말에 뭐 해요?
B: 등산 가요. 같이 갈래요?
What are you doing this weekend? / Going hiking. Want to come?

Small talk
Me too
Casual: 나도.
A: 저 커피 중독이에요.
B: 저도요! 하루에 세 잔은 마셔요.
I'm a coffee addict. / Me too! At least three cups a day.

Small talk
Really?
Softer than 진짜요?. Both fine.
🗣 [정말료] ㄴ 첨가 → ㄹㄹ
A: 저 다음 달에 한국 가요.
B: 정말요? 어디로 가요?
I'm going to Korea next month. / Really? Where to?

Small talk
See you again
또 = again. 내일 봐요 = see you tomorrow.
A: 오늘 재밌었어요. 또 봐요!
B: 네, 연락할게요.
Today was fun. See you again! / Yes, I'll be in touch.

Small talk
Goodbye (to someone leaving)
가세요 = go well. Say it when THEY are leaving.
A: 저 먼저 갈게요. 안녕히 계세요.
B: 네, 안녕히 가세요.
I'll head out first. Goodbye (stay well). / Bye (go well).

Small talk
Goodbye (to someone staying)
계세요 = stay well. Say it when YOU are leaving.
A: 저 이만 가 볼게요. 안녕히 계세요.
B: 네, 조심히 가세요.
I should get going. Goodbye. / Okay, get home safe.

Small talk
I'll be in touch
ㄹ게요 = I'll (promise). 연락 = contact.
🗣 [열라칼게요] 유음화, 격음화
A: 다음에 또 봐요.
B: 네, 연락할게요!
See you next time. / Yes, I'll be in touch!

Food & ordering
mul
water
물 주세요 = water, please.
예: 물 한 잔 주세요.
A glass of water, please.

Café & convenience store
One iced Americano, please
아아 (a-a) = iced Americano slang. 뜨아 = hot Americano.
A: 주문하시겠어요?
B: 아이스 아메리카노 한 잔 주세요.
Ready to order? / One iced Americano, please.

Café & convenience store
What sizes do you have?
Most cafés: 톨 / 그란데 / 벤티 or 레귤러 / 라지.
🗣 [사이즈 뭐 이써요] 연음
A: 사이즈 뭐 있어요?
B: 톨, 그란데, 벤티 있어요.
What sizes do you have? / Tall, grande, venti.

Café & convenience store
For here? (they ask)
Answer: 네, 먹고 갈게요 (for here) / 포장이요 (to go).
A: 드시고 가세요?
B: 아니요, 포장이요.
For here? / No, to go.

Café & convenience store
Do you have a points card? (they ask)
Answer: 아니요, 괜찮아요 = no thanks.
🗣 [정닙 되세요] 비음화
A: 적립 되세요?
B: 아니요, 괜찮아요.
Do you have a points card? / No, that's okay.

Café & convenience store
Please heat it up
Convenience store 도시락 and 삼각김밥. 데우다 = to heat.
A: 이거 데워 주세요.
B: 네, 1분 걸려요.
Please heat this up. / Sure, it takes a minute.

Café & convenience store
Do you need a bag? (they ask)
Answer: 네 / 아니요. Bags cost ~100원.
🗣 [봉투 피료하세요] 연음
A: 봉투 필요하세요?
B: 네, 하나 주세요.
Do you need a bag? / Yes, one please.

Café & convenience store
I'll pay by card
현금으로 = by cash. Tap, no signature needed.
A: 현금이요, 카드요?
B: 카드로 할게요.
Cash or card? / Card.

Directions & transport
here / over there
거기 (geogi) = there (near you).

Time & days
oneul
today
오늘 뭐 해요? = what are you doing today?
예: 오늘 날씨 좋네요.
The weather is nice today.

Time & days
naeil
tomorrow
내일 봐요 = see you tomorrow.
A: 내일 뭐 해요?
B: 내일은 쉬어요. 왜요?
What are you doing tomorrow? / I'm off tomorrow. Why?

Time & days
jigeum
now
지금 몇 시예요? = what time is it now?
A: 지금 몇 시예요?
B: 두 시 반이에요.
What time is it now? / Half past two.

Time & days
What time is it?
몇 = how many; 시 = o'clock.
🗣 [멷 시예요] 받침 → ㄷ
A: 지금 몇 시예요?
B: 아홉 시 십 분이에요.
What time is it? / 9:10.

Numbers in the wild
4,500 won
Sino-Korean: 사천오백. 원 = won.

Weather & feelings
How's the weather?
날씨 = weather. 어때요 = how is it.
A: 서울 날씨가 어때요?
B: 오늘은 춥고 미세먼지도 심해요.
How's the weather in Seoul? / Cold today, and the fine dust is bad.

Weather & feelings
It's raining
비 = rain. 우산 있어요? = do you have an umbrella?
A: 밖에 비가 와요?
B: 네, 우산 가져가세요.
Is it raining outside? / Yes, take an umbrella.

Weather & feelings
I'm tired
Most-used feeling word in Korea.
A: 피곤해 보여요.
B: 네, 어제 잠을 못 잤어요.
You look tired. / Yeah, I couldn't sleep last night.

Weather & feelings
I'm bored
심심하다. 놀자! fixes it.
A: 심심해요.
B: 그럼 영화 볼까요?
I'm bored. / Then shall we watch a movie?

Doctor & pharmacy
Where is a pharmacy?
Green cross sign. Many open late; 편의점 sells basics.
A: 약국 어디예요?
B: 저 건물 1층에 있어요.
Where is a pharmacy? / On the first floor of that building.

Doctor & pharmacy
I have a headache
아프다 = to hurt. 배가 아파요 = stomachache.
A: 어디가 아프세요?
B: 머리가 아파요. 열도 있어요.
Where does it hurt? / My head hurts. I have a fever too.

Doctor & pharmacy
Do you have painkillers?
타이레놀 is understood everywhere.
🗣 [진통제 이써요] 연음
A: 진통제 있어요?
B: 네, 이거 식후에 드세요.
Do you have painkillers? / Yes, take these after a meal.

Doctor & pharmacy
I have an allergy
땅콩 알레르기 = peanut allergy. Say it before ordering too.
🗣 [알레르기 이써요] 연음
A: 알레르기 있으세요?
B: 네, 땅콩 알레르기 있어요.
